flags.message: Footer method is settled as a mix (some pockets saw-cut through the existing pad, some hand-dug) but no source gives the split and no concrete saw is priced in the JBD equipment; each cut pocket is ~1.5h at the rate card plus saw rental, so groundwork carries a null 'footer_pad_cut_count' and is under-sized until Will confirms the layout.

Post/footer count: proposal (8) posts with 8 footers governs per canon, but the presentation p.3 plan draws only 7 '6X6 POST' footing symbols at ~7' c/c along a 41'-9" line. If the field layout is 7, groundwork and post-set effort drop ~12%; sized at 8.

Ceiling is settled as roof-cavity batt + Level 3 drywall (430 sf each), but neither the proposal nor the JBD prices it: JBD carries 'no ceiling drywall' and 7h of wall-only insulation. The drywall bucket is now ~46% overhead work on existing shed rafters (strapping/venting not described), so JBD's 65h is not a ceiling for this scope — anchor to 934 sf takeoff with an overhead premium and add ~430 sf of batt outside JBD hours.

House-side wall is settled as exposed brick with no drywall, so the JBD's 344 sf of house-wall drywall is stale; the sheet count (30) survives only because the 430 sf ceiling replaces it. Presentation p.4 'Drywall over brick' is superseded.

Openings are settled at 6 stock 36x60 windows + 1 stock 36x80 door ordered before demo; the presentation p.4 still tags 7 windows (incl. 2×5050DH) and a 6568 double door on the house wall (existing opening, no work). Sized at 6+1; the presentation counts are stale, not competing.

Presentation renders show a railed deck, exterior stairs, brick-wrapped posts and Option-2 interior finishes; all are settled as NOT contracted (Options 1 and 2 declined, deck/stairs render-only). Nothing is sized for them — and no egress from the elevated room other than through the house exists in the contract.

JBD 455 labor-hours reads hot against the physical takeoff: 87h floor system for 430 sf, 48h demo for a 430 sf room, 69h walls for 63 LF, 65h drywall for 30 sheets. Elevated/occupied/scaffold access justifies the canon +20-25% premium, but sizing should anchor to takeoff quantities and the rate card, citing the JBD only as a ceiling.

JBD double-counts WRB labor (6h sheathing+WRB line plus a separate 3h WRB line) and double-prices the 3 dump runs (material $1,350 and equipment $1,350); the hours-side duplication (3h) should not be inherited.

JBD carries zero hours for permits and inspections although the proposal price 'includes permitting' and IRC 2018/NEC compliance; canon expects ~2h per inspection visit — add ~5 visits (footing, framing, electrical rough, mechanical, insulation/final) outside the JBD totals.

Wall height (8 ft) and post height (~10 ft) come only from the JBD, not the proposal or drawings; the retained shed roof fixes the wall height and the sloped lot means post lengths vary — field measurement should confirm before framing package order.

Scaffold is priced at only 2 days for the underside soffit (430 sf overhead), 63 LF of siding, and roof tie-in flashing on a sloped lot; with house access settled as the crew path, the exterior scope likely needs scaffold standing for the length of cladding_roof, not 2 days, and canon bills erect/strike (~4-8 crew-h per mobilization) explicitly.

Subpanel conversion is contingent on the existing fused disconnect being sound and legally usable as a subpanel (JBD PM note); a replacement subpanel would be an add. Main service is 200A per project answer, so capacity is not the concern — panel condition is.

Material handling through the occupied house (settled access route) is real hours per canon but appears nowhere in the JBD; demo, framing, siding and window buckets should carry the elevated/occupied premium rather than absorb it silently.

Allowance selections (siding profile/color, mini-split BTU/location, fixtures) are unmade and no lead times are stated; windows/door are settled as stock and ordered pre-demo, but canon still forbids scheduling before final selections — the 2027-03-01 start assumes the remaining selections close well ahead.

Several JBD sections straddle sequence components ('framing' = floor system covers structural framing + soffit cladding + floor batt; excavation_foundation covers footers + posts/beam; roof integration is part framing, part flashing). Splits above are by the JBD's own line-item hours, not equal halves. The deck, fireplace_structure, fireplace_finish, retrofit_work and concrete_landscape components receive nothing — none are in scope.
